summary: Backend-only testing per request. All 11 pytest tests PASSED (100%). Verified the GIF list-endpoint contract: /api/memes, /api/memes/explore, and /api/users/{username}/memes now return full image_base64 (starts with 'data:image/gif') for items with media_type=='gif', while non-GIF items correctly omit image_base64 (perf contract preserved). Verified GIF upload → immediate re-list flow: uploaded a synthetic 2-frame animated GIF, POST /api/memes returned 200 with media_type='gif', and the newly created GIF appears in /api/memes?limit=50 and /api/users/missbrittanyb/memes with full image_base64. Single-item /api/memes/{id} still returns full image_base64. Regression tests for /api/reports (POST + admin GET) and /api/users/{username}/block (POST/DELETE toggle + profile.is_blocked field) all pass. Real production data snapshot: /api/memes?limit=50 -> 13 GIFs (all with image_base64) + 37 non-GIFs (all without); /api/memes/explore?limit=50 -> 2/2 GIFs populated, 48/48 non-GIFs skipped; /api/users/missbrittanyb/memes -> 12/12 GIFs populated. The backend display-side of the reported bug ('not seeing moving gifs in the library') is fully resolved server-side. The 'can't upload moving gifs' side is an iOS Photos-picker issue that can only be validated in TestFlight and is out of scope for this sandbox.
action_items: No backend action required — GIF list contract works as designed on real data (13/13, 2/2, 12/12 GIFs populated).

For the 'can't upload moving gifs' side of the user report: this cannot be reproduced from a sandbox because it involves the iOS Photos picker returning static image data for animated GIFs. Main agent should verify ImagePicker on the mobile client uses `mediaTypes: ['images']` with `allowsEditing: false` and reads the file bytes rather than the picker's re-encoded preview. On iOS 14+ the picker often returns a JPEG derivative for animated PH assets unless `PHPickerFilter.images` + direct asset resource reading is used.
Optional perf: /api/memes issues N+1 queries for usernames (one users.find_one per meme). Not a bug, but consider a $lookup / bulk fetch when meme list grows.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_memes/explore_memes/get_user_memes all perform a two-step query: (1) list without image_base64, (2) fetch image_base64 only for gif ids. Correct and efficient pattern.

MemeListItem.image_base64 defaults to None — pydantic serializes it in the JSON. Consider adding `model_config = ConfigDict(exclude_none=True)` or per-field exclude if you want to strictly omit the key for non-GIFs (currently it appears as null, which the tests correctly treat as 'not populated'). Frontend logic that does `item.image_base64 || item.thumbnail_base64` works either way.
N+1 username lookups in get_memes/explore_memes loop (see server.py ~695-701 and ~817-824).
server.py is 2089 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline; recommend splitting into routers (auth, memes, users, reports).

rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: The list endpoints (/api/memes, /api/memes/explore, /api/users/{u}/memes) originally used a Mongo projection of {image_base64: 0} to keep grid queries cheap. That optimization stripped the animated GIF data too, so the frontend fell back to thumbnail_base64 — a static JPEG of the first frame generated by generate_thumbnail() at upload time — making every GIF appear frozen in every grid (Home, Explore, User Profile, own Profile). FIX (already applied in server.py at get_memes ~L680, explore_memes ~L804, get_user_memes ~L516): after the projection-stripped list query, collect ids where media_type=='gif' and issue a second targeted find({id:{$in:gif_ids}}, {image_base64:1}) to hydrate only those items. Non-GIFs remain lightweight. Tests confirm 13/13, 2/2, 12/12 GIFs are hydrated in real production data and 0 non-GIFs leak the field. REPRODUCTION (fixed): curl -sS $BASE/api/memes?limit=50 | jq '[.[] | select(.media_type=="gif") | .image_base64 | startswith("data:image/gif")] | all' -> true. MITIGATION for iOS upload side (still unverified in sandbox): ensure the mobile ImagePicker reads the original asset resource (PHAssetResource) rather than the transcoded preview so the picker doesn't hand back a JPEG when the user selects an animated GIF.
